correctness.rationale: For C the generated order has only the diagonal and pairs a^n b <= b a^n because every generator bottom starts with a and every top starts with b, so no nontrivial generator chain can continue. The same first-letter barrier applies to the tuple generators defining D. Thus p=(a^2 b,a) and q=(b a^2,a) satisfy p<=q componentwise in T(C), while p is neither q nor a D-generator bottom because its second coordinate a is not a^n b; hence p not<=q in D. Separately, lambda_{m+n} follows from lambda_n in left context a^m and lambda_m in right context a^n, so lambda_2 and lambda_3 derive every lambda_n for n>=2. A fresh independent recursion checked these derivations through n=100; the global proof is the semigroup decomposition by 2 and 3, not the finite test.
